text:
**B1 First Interview - Petah Tikva Branch**

Hey everyone,

We had our first B1 interview, and as I always find it helpful to read about others' experiences, I would like to share ours as well!

We submitted our documents in October 2025. One week after that, my Israeli partner got an email saying that we could hand in the documents in person with an appointment on November 5th. At the appointment, the clerk looked at some of the documents and scheduled our first interview. He said because it was pretty busy right now, our appointment would be at the end of March (something like the 24th or 29th). He also asked me if I wanted a German translator for the interview.

In December I wanted to see my family for Christmas, so my partner sent an email to our clerk and asked what we should do. He said we could send him an email with an official request, and once it was accepted, we could come to Misrad Hapnim to get a one-time re-entry visa. That's what we did, and at that time my B2 tourist visa was also extended until April 16th because we already had our interview scheduled for the end of March.

In March, our interview got canceled because of the war. My Israeli partner sent an email to our clerk directly to ask about our appointment. One or two days later, we received a response with a new appointment on July 7th. The B2 visa got automatically extended for 3 months.

On July 7th, we had our interview scheduled for 10 am but still waited about an hour. Then it was our turn, and he said that I would start. I thought there would be a German translator present in the room, but it was via a phone call and at the normal desk with all the other people around. It was a bit weird, so for anyone feeling confident enough to do the interview in English, I imagine that might be a bit more comfortable. I will attach the questions down below. After about 30 minutes, I needed to sign a few papers. I asked if I should read them, but he said no. Then it was my partner's turn. After another 30 minutes, the clerk told us that was it and that he needed to confirm the answers with his manager, so we didn't get the visa right away.

My partner asked how long it would take because my visa only lasted until July 16th. The clerk said it would be fine, and a few hours later he called my partner to say we could pick up the visa 2 days after. He told us to let the workers in Misrad Hapnim know to send us directly to him so we wouldn't have to wait. That's what we did, and after about 10 minutes in Misrad Hapnim, I finally received my B1 visa!

These are the questions we got asked:

- How did we meet?

- Who sent the first message?

- Where was our first meeting?

- How long was the first meeting?

- How did the relationship continue after that?

- When was the first time I visited Israel?

- How long was my first stay here?

- Where did we stay at that time?

- Where do we live now?

- Are we paying rent or do we own the apartment?

- Who pays the bills?

- How many rooms does the apartment have?

- Am I working? If so, where?

- Is my partner working? If so, where?

- Did we study?

- Did we travel in Israel in the last 6 months?

- Have we been abroad?

- Where do we go grocery shopping?

- When was the last time we were at the supermarket and where? (My partner mentioned a short shopping for a few things, and the clerk asked him, "Are you sure there was no bigger grocery shopping recently?" because of my answer.)

- How did we get to Misrad Hapnim today? (We took the bus, so he wanted to know the specific bus line.)

- What did we do for our last birthdays?

- Do we give each other gifts?

- Do we have friends?

- When was the last time we met up with friends?

- What did we do last weekend?

- When was the last time I saw my partner's parents?

- What do we like to do together?

- Do we own a car?

- What are our future plans?

- Do we want to live in Israel? (The clerk also asked my partner why we don't want to live in Germany.)

- How is our health? Are we taking any medication?

I wrote everything down right after the interview, so I believe these were all the questions. My partner also mentioned that our clerk was quite nice compared to others he heard during his interview. In the past we also had some complicated experiences with Misrad Hapnim about other situations, but now in total, our B1 visa experience was smooth and positive. I was pretty nervous before the interview, so I hope this helps someone and makes them feel less anxious about it :)
